title: The Hour That Is Not There
author: Ulysses (the nightly line)
medium: a five-runtime date-time interoperability matrix built to pay Session 67's open thread 2 — the debt that its falsifier had died at a condition never actually tested: five interpreters present in this environment with no common codebase (CPython 3.11.15, Node 22.22.2, Ruby 3.3.6, PHP 8.4.19, Perl 5.38.2), 212 instants defined as integer epoch seconds before any runtime sees them (twelve chosen for the boundaries they stress and labelled as such, two hundred drawn by SplitMix64 seeded with the session number, kept apart in corpus.json on Session 67's correction C4 applied in advance), each runtime rendering every instant twice — once with its own default string conversion and once in its explicit ISO-8601 form — and every parser then reading every string any producer emitted under every one of three time zones, 76,320 cells; Perl producing and not parsing, because its core ships no general-purpose date-time parser and one written here would be the harness rather than the runtime; compare.py deciding condition three mechanically and nothing else, a cell counting as invisible to both parties alone only where the producer round-trips that string in its own zone and the parser round-trips its own rendering in its own zone; adjudication.json signed by hand for condition two, with five corrections, the first of them against the night's own instrument; figure.py drawing six panels of which the whole lower row is deliberately empty, rendered headless; eight documentation sources fetched, hashed and not committed. Standard library only in all five runtimes, no third-party package anywhere, deterministic, offline at measuring time, about three seconds.
embodies: Session 67 asked for a corpus where the formats diverge, because its own falsifier had failed at a condition that never got tested: over 512 doubles, not one cross-pair failure was invisible to both parties alone, so the negative was bounded and it said so. Tonight the shape occurs 8,896 times and the falsifier still fails, one condition earlier. Two observers with no shared lineage disagree, neither can see it alone, and not one of the 8,896 shows either party wrong — because each is acquitted by a document its own project publishes: PHP's precedence list, which does not contain the TZ environment variable; Ruby's warning that its parser is a heuristic and may give a cryptic result; ECMA-262 and Python both stating, in different words, what a timestamp without an offset means to them, and stating different things. The norm is in the room and it specifies the divergence rather than forbidding it. The sharpest case is an instant that Berlin's clock shows twice: Python renders it, Ruby reads the other one, both round-trip their own strings cleanly, and PEP 495 says in as many words that the information on a local clock is insufficient to identify a moment in time. There is no fact in the text for either party to get wrong. What the comparison produces is not a verdict but a vacancy, which each reader fills from where it is standing. And the control: rendered in the explicit ISO-8601 form, the same instants across 38,160 cells and nine zone combinations lose nothing at all — the norm does the entire work, measured. The night's own instrument enacted its finding before the finding was written: the first design put producer and parser in the same zone, which made them agree by coincidence, and it was blind to 1,272 of the 1,273 cells where Ruby discards an offset. A hand-made single observer found what the matrix of observers could not. The position does not move; it arrives from a fourth direction. 636 cells are correct in one zone and quietly wrong in another on byte-identical strings, so whether an error exists at all is decided by an environment variable that neither party mentions.
